hp_driver.text: The Healy Pass has more hairpins than a hairdresser's. I come up here of a Sunday to watch the cars, and the sheep watch me.
God, it's soft out. That's what we say in this country when it's raining so gently you could mistake it for a mood.

hp_miner_guide.text: Those engine houses are Cornish. Cornish miners came over with the steam engines. A fair few stayed and married, and a good few Allihies families still have a Cornish name on the gate.
Daphne du Maurier wrote a novel about it called Hungry Hill, about a family with a mine and a great many feuds. It is not a quiet book.

hp_cable.text: A handful at a time, and no more. The wind has a say, and when the wind says no, we wait. Sure what's the hurry? It's an island.
Dursey is a grand place for a walk. Nobody lives there now. The cows, the sheep and the birds do the housekeeping.

champ_hp_cornish.text: Hello again. Mind the hairpins; they're the only thing on this road with a sense of humour. I came to look at the view and somebody has parked in it.

intro: The Cornish brought the know-how to the copper here, and I brought myself. A rematch, is it? Go on, then.
I've a fair idea what the weather's done to my team, mind.
champ_hp_cornish.win: Well, that's me told. Come back next week and I'll have thought of something.
champ_hp_cornish.tired: Not this week. The sheep complained about the noise last time. Monday, and I'll be ready.
